newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan Jan-July domestic oil sales fell 6.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan Jan-July domestic oil sales fell 6.7 pct.

text.p: Domestic sales of energy products rose to 538,707 tonnes in July of 1996 from 459,715 tonnes for the same month last year, a rise of 17.18 percent, the Confederation of Moroccan Businesses said in its bulletin.
But for the first seven months of this year, sales fell 6.7 percent to 3.254 million tonnes from 3.490 in the same period of 1995, the bulletin said.

Gasoline sales climbed by 2.5 percent in July, attributable to expatriates returning home for summer, but registered a total drop of 3.9 percent to 282,041 tonnes for the first seven months of 1996 against the same period last year.

Diesel sales rose 4.0 percent in July owing to steady activity in agriculture and the road transport of freight. But sales from January to July declined to 1.676 million tonnes from 1.696 million. This was attributed to the laying up of fishing boats during the period to allow fish stocks to recover.

Fuel for power stations shrank to 950,139 tonnes from 1.183 million tonnes in the first seven months, despite an increase of 47,000 tonnes in July due to purchases by electricity utilities following a tax reduction.
Morocco has no oil of its own and imports all its energy, needs mainly from the Gulf countries.
